title: Business English: Using technology at work

vocabulary.meaning: software that helps people work and communicate together
examples: The team uses a collaboration tool to share updates.
A good collaboration tool can reduce unnecessary emails.

vocabulary.meaning: a meeting in which people communicate by live video over the internet
examples: We have a video conference with the London office tomorrow.
Video conferences make remote teamwork easier.

vocabulary.meaning: online storage that allows files to be saved and accessed through the internet
examples: Save the document in the team's cloud storage.
Cloud storage makes it easier to work from different locations.

vocabulary.meaning: the protection of computers, networks, and data from digital attacks
examples: Employees receive regular cybersecurity training.
Strong passwords are a basic part of cybersecurity.

vocabulary.meaning: the amount or quality of work completed in a given time
examples: The new software improved team productivity.
Too many digital tools can sometimes reduce productivity.

vocabulary.meaning: work done away from a traditional office, often from home
examples: Remote work depends heavily on reliable technology.
The company allows remote work two days a week.

vocabulary.meaning: computer programs used to perform tasks
examples: The company upgraded its project-management software.
Employees need training before using new software.

vocabulary.meaning: a piece of electronic equipment such as a phone, tablet, or laptop
examples: Do not leave a work device unlocked in a public place.
Employees can use their own devices for some tasks.

vocabulary.meaning: an ability needed to use digital tools effectively
examples: Basic digital skills are required for most office jobs.
Training helps employees develop new digital skills.

vocabulary.meaning: the use of technology to perform tasks with little human involvement
examples: Automation can save time on repetitive work.
The company automated several reporting tasks.
